problem: Given the width of a tic-tac-toe board, what is the smallest dimension such that X is guaranteed to have a winning strategy?
missing_details: Precise definition of the game board as the d-dimensional hypercube {1,…,n}^d
Turn‐taking rules and identification of X as the first player and O as the second
Exact definition of a “line” (the winning configuration) in the d-dimensional grid
Specification of the draw condition when no line is completed
Clarification that n>1 is assumed (the cases n=1 or d=0 trivial)
refined_question: For each integer n≥2, consider the combinatorial game played by two players X and O on the d-dimensional grid of size n×n×⋯×n (i.e. the set of all d-tuples with entries in {1,…,n}). Players alternate placing their marks (X goes first) in any unoccupied grid cell. A player wins immediately if, after their move, they occupy all n cells of some axis-aligned line (that is, a set of cells obtained by fixing d−1 coordinates and letting the remaining coordinate vary over {1,…,n}). If all n^d cells become filled without either player completing such a line, the game is a draw. Determine, as a function of n, the minimal integer d(n) for which player X has a forced winning strategy.
justification: The Wikipedia article “nᵈ game” states the problem exactly as above but without defining the hypercube grid, turn‐taking, line, or draw condition, all of which are required to make the question self-contained. The original name mentions only width, dimension, and X’s winning strategy, omitting these essential details, so the name alone scores low on completeness (3/10). The refined question incorporates the precise game definition faithful to the canonical source.
